desc:
Drupal multisite and multilingual builds let a larger organization run several sites, several languages and a careful approval chain from one platform. Ecom Swift LLC plans the structure in writing, configures it, and tests it on a staging site before your team takes over.

## What are Drupal multisite and multilingual builds?

A Drupal multisite build runs more than one website from a shared codebase, so updates and improvements are made once. A multilingual build adds translated content, language switching and clear address rules, so each audience reads the site in its own language. An editorial workflow adds roles and states, so a writer cannot publish alone and a reviewer sees only what is ready.

These three ideas often appear together in universities, associations, regional offices and companies with several brands. Each one is available in Drupal, but each needs choices that are hard to reverse once content exists.

## Why structure decisions come first

The costly mistakes in a large Drupal project are made in the first week, not the last. Choosing separate sites when one site with language versions would do doubles the maintenance. Choosing one site when departments need their own control leads to arguments over who can edit what.

We write the architecture down before we build anything. The plan names which content is shared, which content belongs to a single site, which languages are needed and who approves what. You can read it, change it and agree to it, so the build starts from a shared understanding.

## How a good setup improves your team's results

A clear structure saves time and reduces errors. Editors work only in the section they own, so fewer mistakes reach the public. Translators see which pages are waiting for them, so no language falls behind without anyone noticing. A shared codebase means a security fix or a new feature reaches every site at once instead of being repeated by hand.

For visitors, correct language versions and consistent navigation build trust. For search engines, clean language address rules help the right version appear for the right audience.

## What a strong multisite and multilingual setup includes

- A written architecture plan covering sites, languages, roles and shared content.
- Language configuration with a visible language switcher on every page.
- Address rules for each language, using a path prefix or a separate domain.
- Translation enabled for the content types that need it, and left off for those that do not.
- Interface and configuration translation, so menus, buttons and form labels match the page language.
- Editorial roles for writer, reviewer and publisher, each with only the permissions they need.
- A draft to published workflow with content moderation states.
- Rules for shared content and site specific content across multiple sites.
- Access control by section, so a department cannot change another department's pages.
- Written setup notes and an admin guide for your own team.

## What we do

First we review your goals and agree the structure with you in writing. Next we build on a staging site, configure the languages and translation settings, and create the roles and workflow states. For larger packages we set up the shared codebase with the extra sites and the rules for what is shared between them.

We then test each role by logging in as a writer, a reviewer and a publisher, and we check every language version on desktop and phone. The Basic, Standard and Premium packages differ in the number of languages, content types and sites, and whether a training session is included. When you approve staging, we help move the setup to your live hosting.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Decide who owns each section of the site before the build starts.
- Keep content types simple and reuse them across languages.
- Plan who will translate, since the software organizes translation but does not do it.
- Test the approval chain with real people before launch.
- Keep one written list of roles and what each may do.

**Avoid:**
- Creating a separate site for every small need.
- Giving every editor full administrator rights.
- Translating every content type by default, including ones that never change.
- Launching languages before the translators are ready.
- Skipping staging because the deadline is close.

## Who this is for

This service suits a university or association that needs one site per faculty or chapter, with shared branding. It also suits a company expanding into new countries that needs translated pages and a review step before anything goes live. A communications team that wants writers separated from publishers will also benefit.

## What we need from you

Send a short description of your sites, languages and teams, and a list of the roles you want. Tell us where your Drupal site is hosted and whether a staging copy exists. We never need your password: access is given to us as a developer or administrator user in your own account, which you can remove at any time. Once your order is in, you get a brief checklist from us, and we send progress notes right up to the handover.
